Inventory and buying stay where they are: TradeGecko tracked stock across warehouses and raised the purchase orders for your suppliers. We do neither, so that work stays in the inventory software you rely on now.
Billing stays the way you run it: TradeGecko's store took card payments and showed customers their invoices. Our app has no checkout and takes no payment: you invoice and collect as you do today.

The next system change leaves ordering alone: Our app is not tied to any inventory product. If you change that software again, restaurants keep ordering in the same app from the same guides; how their orders get into the new system is something we check with you in a demo.

@graph.name: Does VoiceOrder Solutions work as a TradeGecko alternative?

acceptedAnswer.text: As an alternative to TradeGecko's store, yes: your restaurants get an app to say each order in, check it and send it. For stock, purchasing, warehouses and accounting, no: those are jobs for inventory software, and ours works beside the one you run.

@graph.name: Would VoiceOrder Solutions be better than TradeGecko?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only at one job: letting a chef read out the order, then confirm each item on a phone. TradeGecko did far more, from stock and purchasing to warehouses, and its store orders went straight into its own records.

Intuit bought TradeGecko in 2020 and renamed it QuickBooks Commerce. It stopped taking new customers in June 2021 and was retired in stages: many users lost it in June 2022, and the last version closed after August 31, 2023. If you are looking for a TradeGecko alternative now, the stock side may already be settled.

@graph.name: Will orders go straight into our stock system?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how each order is sent. VoiceOrder Solutions is a separate product, not part of any stock system. If yours takes orders over EDI or an API, an order can load with no retyping; the demo shows whether it does. By email, it arrives as a file listing every item the chef approved. Your team still enters it, but there is no call to take, write down and read back. Customers, stock and invoices stay on record where they are now; we hold each account's order guide with its prices, plus the orders sent through the app. Phoned orders get no number from us, while every order sent from the app is numbered and timed.

@graph.name: Can restaurants still browse a catalog and pay by card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not in our app. It has no catalog to browse, no checkout and no card payment. If browsing and paying online matter to your customers, an online store does that better, and if your current stock software has one, keep it. Our app is for the restaurant that wants to say what it needs and be done.

@graph.name: Can the app mishear an item?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can happen: the app turns speech into items from that account's list, and it may pick the wrong one. The chef sees the full list before sending and can swap or delete anything. If a mistake still reaches you, you sort it out the way you handle any order mix-up today.

@graph.name: How much is it, and how fast can we start?

acceptedAnswer.text: We quote each business and list no prices online, so ask us on the demo call. To get started, you send us each account's usual items, often as a spreadsheet; we load them in and set up each account. Your restaurants download the app, and most send a first order the same day. Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours.

@graph.name: Where do the TradeGecko details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From TradeGecko's own pages as saved by the Internet Archive in June 2020 (home, B2B store, mobile sales app and pricing), and from Intuit's notices about QuickBooks Commerce ending, all reviewed on 9 November 2026. Spot something wrong? Write to us and we will fix it.
